modules.module_title: Carry out preparatory activity for the expedition

pcs.pc_description: collate work instructions, details of the expedition and its difficulty level from the organizer.
obtain and assess detailed information about the student/client's age, gender, health issues(if any), special requests and past experience in mountaineering (if any).
review all technical information for the expedition and share the same with the participants.
prepare a list of all the equipment and logistics required for the expedition.
supervise the tasks carried out by the assistant instructor, high altitude trekking guide, high altitude porter and kitchen staff for expedition planning and preparation.
identify skills that need to be taught based on the technical requirements of the final expedition and prepare a training schedule for the team.
identify the training area while ensuring it has all the elements needed for the training program.
organize assessment sheets to grade the participants on their skills learnt.

coordinate with and assist the rest of the team members (high altitude trekking guide, high altitude porter, kitchen staff) to complete transportation requirements, booking porter/ponies and arranging for any last-minute supplies for the expedition.

modules.module_title: Conduct pre-expedition logistics and equipment check

pcs.pc_description: coordinate with transporters, porters/ponies, suppliers, local police, hospitals and district office and pass on the trip information to them if required.

inspect the condition and certification of equipment such as kernmantle ropes, harnesses, helmets, climbing shoes, snow boots, crampons, mittens, gaiters, carabiners, pulley, belay devices, slings, tape slings, pitons, ice axe, etc.

ensure that sufficient numbers and sizes of equipment such as harnesses, mittens, climbing shoes, helmets, snow boots, crampons, ice axe, helmets, gaiters and backpacks, etc., are available for the guests.

create a checklist (on computer) of all the personal mountaineering equipment (harness, helmet, wind/water resistant jackets, climbing shoes, ladders , snow boots, crampons, gaiters sleeping bags, ice axe, etc.) to be issued to the participants and a checklist of personal belongings they need to carry for the expedition.
make logbook entries of all the equipment being used, along with the serial number and quantity of each equipment.

modules.module_title: Prepare the participants for the expedition

pcs.pc_description: welcome the students/clients in a friendly and approachable manner.
distribute the equipment and personal gear checklists to each participant.

assist the students/clients in trying out the harness, helmets, wind/water resistant jackets, climbing shoes, snow boots, crampons and backpacks according to their respective sizes and adjust their fittings.
review all participants’ personal gear list to ensure that they're not over or under packed and assist them in packing.
issue any equipment provided by the expedition organizer e.g., sleeping bags, mats, rucksacks, etc.
brief the students/clients about the training and expedition schedule.
assist the students/clients for any last-minute purchases.
brief and demonstrate the ABCDE’s (Accessibility, Balance, Compress, Dry, Everything inside) of backpacking.
sensitize female participants about female hygiene products and their proper disposal in the wilderness.
review each student's/client's medical condition and level of fitness.

pcs.pc_description: ensure that the students/clients have signed the indemnity waivers.
coordinate with the other team members to ensure everything is in place – porters/ponies, vehicles, general camp equipment.
ensure that camp crew departs first with all the equipment and provisions to set up the first camp or the training camp as required.
coordinate with the trekking guide to ensure that there are adequate quantity of packed lunches, snacks and drinking water.

modules.module_title: Conduct the training and assist in the expedition

pcs.pc_description: assist and share responsibility with the trekking guide to guide the students/clients to the rock craft, ice craft and snow craft site (while hiking or in vehicles).

create a safe training environment by assessing crag or mountain to determine a safe, efficient and effective solution and conduct the training activity in a safe manner as per risk assessment protocols e.g., how to wear equipment, staying hydrated, etc.

ensure training level is based on technical difficulties anticipated for the expedition eg., use of ropes, self arresting, use of pitons and ice axe on an ice wall, walking on soft snow with snow boots, on hard snow with the help of crampons and choose climbing routes from easy to moderate to challenging.
ensure to use maps and stick to the route that was planned, unless there is some major hazard preventing you from doing so.
plan day by day route selection as per the group dynamics.
organize all the equipment on a flat surface over a tarpaulin and demonstrate how to wear and remove PPE (harness, helmet, mittens, climbing shoes, snow boots, crampons, gaiters).
conduct the training on different techniques for using mountaineering equipment.

train and assist students/clients on different pitches (short, long and multi-pitch), chimney climbing, lead climbing and while navigating through technical areas such as glaciers, loose rock areas and crevasses.
help the expedition leader choose climbing parties as per personal attributes of the students/clients.
assist climbers during the expedition and summit attempts and ensure they are accurately utilizing the training given to them so they can achieve their goals.
provide information about the local culture, traditions, history, religious and mythological beliefs followed in the mountains of the particular area.
maintain a daily log of equipment used, incidents or injuries (if any) and learning progress of each student/client.
assess the progress of the learners and exclude /include them in advanced training or expedition attempt accordingly.
take decisions to discontinue an activity due to any incident or changing weather conditions.
document photos and/or videos of the trip with their phone camera or with the company provided one such as GoPro/DSLR, ensuring not to take selfies.
provide on the spot first-aid during emergencies.
use satellite phones/two way radios to promptly coordinate with the evacuation and rescue team.
maintain calm and be composed if a student/client is stuck while doing the activity and in case of emergencies.
offer help to persons with disabilities when asked for.
accommodate persons with disabilities in the activities, as far as possible, without compromising safety.
adhere to “minimum impact” policies and not throw/burn non bio-degradable waste materials such as wrappers and plastic bottles into the valley, cliffs, trails or any of the activity areas.
ensure to not cause damage to the fragile habitats and environments (animal life, flora and fauna) found there.
ensure all waste is disposed appropriately into garbage bins.
educate female students/clients about the disposal procedure of their personal hygiene products.

modules.module_title: Equipment pack up and submission of trip report

pcs.pc_description: ensure all the equipment used on the expedition is counted and packed.
maintain a record of the total duration the climbing ropes were used for, any loss or damage to the equipment and incidents (if any) in the logbook.
complete the grading for the students in the group on their overall mountaineering techniques and behavioral skills.
conduct a debrief session for the expedition with the team and participants.

create an expedition report with details such as – number of participants with their names and age, activity location of each craft, mountain villages and other landmarks on the trails taken, duration of the expedition, mountaineering techniques taught, challenges/hazards faced, incidents (if any), highlights and low points of the expedition, elevation gained, total distance covered, peaks climbed (if any), suggestions and any inputs for future trips etc.
complete all formalities with the organizer/Indian Mountaineering Foundation (IMF) e.g., settle accounts, hand over all equipment, reports, log books, etc.

modules.module_title: Ensure that all safety measures are taken

pcs.pc_description: ensure that all participants and crew are insured for evacuation and hospitalisation.
identify ailments, contact the appointed doctor and take appropriate action.
ensure that the entire crew is informed in case of any chronic ailments or allergies in the group.
perform a basic risk assessment of each activity area during rock, ice and snow craft before starting the activity.
ensure that only standardized and certified equipment is used (UIAA or CE certified).
ensure that the climbing ropes (static and dynamic) used for the activity are free of any type of damage such as cuts, rips or tears, thin bits, fat bits etc.
follow globally recognized anchor systems for rock climbing and abseiling e.g., SERENE/ERNEST.

instruct the students/clients to wait at a safe location away from any cliffs, under the rock face or ice wall, while wearing the safety gear and until all activity related instructions are given and their turn arrives.
instruct students/clients with long hair to tie up hair properly to fit below the helmet, tie up loose clothing and remove any jewellery while rock climbing and in all of the ropes course elements.
ensure to self- secure before starting the activity.

instruct on the communication protocols e.g., belayer ready?, I am climbing, climb on, etc.) and rescue signals to be followed in case of an emergency between instructor and participants during, between or after finishing the activity.
ensure to check the fitting of the PPE (Personal Protective Equipment) on the students/clients before commencing the activity.

instruct the students/clients to wear waterproof gloves and wind/waterproof jackets while ice climbing and have sunglasses on while traversing through glaciers to prevent frost bites and snow blindness respectively.
instruct the students/clients to remain hydrated under sun exposed areas and ensure that all staff and participants get enough rest and take meals properly.
ensure to carry a detailed evacuation/emergency plan, for each day of the expedition including contact numbers of emergency services.
ensure that evacuation routes are easily accessible.
oversee that there are enough first aid kits with adequate supplies for all participants, oxygen cylinder, HAPO bag, stretcher/spinal board before starting the expedition.
watch for signs and symptoms of high-altitude sickness, fatigue or other infections and take the required action promptly.
ensure that everyone in the team is aware of the emergency plan within one's purview.

modules.module_title: Respond to emergency situations and manage disasters

pcs.pc_description: respond promptly to emergency situations for eg. manage guest movement away from any emergency and provide first aid, CPR and oxygen whenever required.
choose camp site carefully to safeguard from avalanche, treefall, rockfall, flooding and lightning.
establish communication and organize air and land rescue in case of a disaster.
evacuate people from danger zone and provide shelter till rescue arrives, in case of any disaster/emergency.
organise for food, provisions and medicines and instruct the cook to improvise menu to ensure supplies are used judiciously during disaster situations.
deal with all eventualities in a calm and composed manner.
handle the media and family members of the injured person in a sensitive manner in case of a serious accident.
